History of Present Illness:
___ F with DM, HTN; admit with CP and dyspnea.  CP began 
yesterday afternoon with associated L upper arm tingling in the 
evening.  Began all of a sudden at rest.  Today CP worse, also 
associated with dyspnea noted with speech this AM, so came to 
ED.  Pain is substernal and slightly to the left, no radiation 
but + arm tingling yesterday as above.  Describes as grabbing 
sensation this AM.  Worse with deep breath.  Says she has had CP 
and SOB before separately without clear etiology, never together 
that she can remember though.  Did not worsen when walking to 
the T this AM.  No N/V/diaphoresis, no cough.  No sick contacts, 
URI symptoms.  Did note R calf pain.  No unusual stressors.

flat surfaces, stairs x 1 flight, no other exercise. + smoker 
""less than one pack per month"".  Stress test last ___.
.

Brief Hospital Course:
A/P: ___ F with DM, HTN; admit with CP, dyspnea; admit for ___ 
and ___ control.
.
# Chest pain and dyspnea: x 24 hours without relief; waxing and 
waning.  Given timecourse, no worsening with exertion, unlikely 
to be cardiac, though does have risk factors (DM, smoking).  ECG 
unchanged, and cardiac enzymes were negative.  Last stress was 
less than 2 months ago, however, given ongoing symptoms and risk 
factors she did have another exercise MIBI which showed good 
exercise tolerance and normal perfusion.  PE was unlikely given 
normal Ddimer and was further ruled out with normal V/Q scan. 
She had had similar symptoms before, just not both CP and SOB 
together.  Ddx other than above included GERD, anxiety, 
pericarditis, costrochondritis/MSK.  She also had a question of 
asthma in her history and had wheezing on exam.  She was started 
on neb treatments and noted significant improvement in chest 
pain.  It is possible that pain was perhaps related to reactive 
airways and URI.  She was chest pain free at discharge, and will 
further followup with her PCP; also have PFTs upcoming.
.
# Wheeze: Developed on exam, though no clear history of asthma.  
Is in the process of being worked up for asthma though, with 
upcoming PFTs.  Given nebs as above, and will continue use of 
albuterol inhaler as needed as an outpatient.
.
# HTN: Elevated BP in ED, now under better control.  Reports 
taking all her meds as supposed to.  Her home regimen of 
amlodipine, eplerenone, HCTZ continued.
. 
# DM: Well controlled per past HA1Cs.  Continued glyburide plus 
SS coverage.
.
# Neck fullness: ? subclavicular adenopathy vs fullness, 
?thyromegaly.  TSH was normal, thyroid ultrasound showing normal 
thyroid size.
.
# CKD: baseline ___ slightly above baseline tonight.  Got 
IVFs in ED, and improved with this.  CKD likely ___ DM and HTN.
.

Discharge Instructions:
You were admitted with chest pains and shortness of breath.  We 
are not sure exactly what is causing your symptoms, but it may 
be related to possible asthma.  We checked your lab work and 
other studies and we are confident that you did not have a heart 
attack or blood clot in your lungs.  You also had a stress test, 
which was normal.
.
Please return to the hospital or call your doctor if you have 
worsening breathing, recurrence of chest pain, fever, cough, or 
any new symptoms that you are concerned about.
.
Take your medications as prescribed.  We have made no changes to 
your medication regimen.  You should continue to use your 
albuterol inhaler as needed for wheezing and shortness of 
breath.
